issues.description: The solution's common Person model uses the field/getter names 'givenName' / getGivenName(), whereas the problem statement and the template Person model use 'firstName' / getFirstName(). Other solution classes (PersonService, PersonScene) still refer to getFirstName() and property 'firstName'. This name mismatch between the Person class and the rest of the code is a structural inconsistency that will cause compilation/runtime issues and confuse students, because the template and problem expect 'firstName' while the solution's model uses 'givenName'.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Person model consistent across all artifacts. Restore the field/getter/setter names to 'firstName' (getFirstName/setFirstName) in src/common/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java of the solution, or alternatively update all usages (PersonService, PersonScene, templates, and the problem statement) to use 'givenName' consistently. Preferably align with the problem statement and template by using 'firstName'.

issues.description: The Person model's first name field is named inconsistently: the problem statement and the template use the identifier 'firstName' (Person.firstName / getFirstName/setFirstName), while the solution's common Person class uses 'givenName' (getGivenName/setGivenName). This mismatch breaks the conceptual mapping for students (the requirement describes firstName but the final model uses givenName) and also creates a code-level inconsistency because server-side code in the solution (PersonService) still refers to setFirstName/getFirstName. Students will be unable to reliably map the problem requirements to the provided/common model and may face compilation errors or confusion about which property to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single, consistent identifier for the same concept across all artifacts. Prefer changing the solution's Person class to use 'firstName' (rename givenName -> firstName and update getGivenName/setGivenName to getFirstName/setFirstName) so it matches the problem statement and template; also ensure all references (e.g. PersonService, controllers, views) use getFirstName/setFirstName. Alternatively, if 'givenName' is preferred, update the problem statement, template, and all code to consistently use 'givenName'.
